ledger.x: 1513: Koli Tenguella wrests Futa Toro from Jolof and founds the Denianke state.
by 1600: the Kingdom of Jolof pays tribute to the Denianke.
by 1600: Waalo pays tribute to the Denianke.
by 1600: Saloum pays tribute to the Denianke.
by 1600: Gajaaga pays tribute to the Denianke.
by 1600: Diarra pays tribute to the Denianke.
early 17th century: Cayor becomes a Denianke tributary.
1776: the Torodbe overthrow the Denianke and found the Imamate of Futa Toro under Sulayman Bal and Abdul Qadir ibn Hammadi (Abdul Kader).
1776: the Denianke tribute from jolof-kingdom ends with the dynasty, a bridge.
1776: the Denianke tribute from waalo ends with the dynasty, a bridge.
1776: the Denianke tribute from saloum ends with the dynasty, a bridge.
1776: the Denianke tribute from gajaaga ends with the dynasty, a bridge.
1776: the Denianke tribute from diarra ends with the dynasty, a bridge.
1776: the Denianke tribute from cayor ends with the dynasty, a bridge.
1859: the Imamate of Futa Toro ends.

wars.name: Torodbe revolution of Sulayman Bal
wars.outcome: A jihad from 1769 to 1776; "In 1776 the Torodbe overthrew the ruling Denianke Dynasty."

wars.name: Futa Toro wars with the Wolof states
wars.outcome: Abdul Kader was "defeated and captured when he attacked the Wolof states of Cayor and Waalo around 1797"; no border change.

wars.name: Futa Toro and the French
wars.outcome: Umar Tall, whose recruiting ground was Futa Toro, was defeated at Médine in 1857; in 1860 he recognised French supremacy in Futa Toro; France annexed it in 1859 (the page).

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier; the state was a river-valley strip with tributaries and a moving capital.
